short: The Imperial Japanese Navy's principal carrier fighter, possessing exceptional range and manoeuvrability.
full:
The Mitsubishi A6M, universally known as the Zero, was introduced in 1940 and immediately established itself as one of the most capable carrier-based fighters in the world. Designed to meet demanding specifications for range and agility, it achieved its remarkable performance by eliminating armour protection and self-sealing fuel tanks. During the first year of the Pacific War, the Zero completely outclassed early Allied fighters, playing a central role in the attack on Pearl Harbor and Japan's subsequent rapid expansion across Asia.

As the war progressed, the Zero's design limitations became a fatal liability. New Allied fighters like the F6F Hellcat and F4U Corsair used superior speed and heavy armour to negate its manoeuvrability, while the loss of experienced Japanese pilots compounded the growing technological disparity. By 1944, it was largely obsolete as an air superiority fighter, and in the final months of the conflict, thousands were expended in kamikaze attacks against the Allied fleet.
